battle.title: Line Up Showdown
battle.description: Survive a rush of enqueue and dequeue questions where first in means first out.

questions.text: You enqueue A, then B, then C into a queue and dequeue once. What comes out?
options: C, because the newest item leaves first
A, because the first item added leaves first
B, because the middle item is removed
Whichever has the smallest letter, regardless of insertion order
questions.answer: A, because the first item added leaves first
questions.explanation: A queue is FIFO, so the oldest item is served first. C would be the answer for a stack, which is the common mix-up.
poll removes the front (1), offer(4) adds at the back, so the queue is [2, 3, 4]: peek is 2 and size is 3. Answering 1 forgets that poll removed it.

questions.text: A print server must print documents in the order they were submitted. Which structure fits best?
options: A priority queue sorted by file name
A hash set of print jobs
questions.explanation: First come, first served is FIFO, which is a queue. A stack would print the newest job first and starve older ones.
Each round moves the front to the back and then removes the next front: [1,2,3,4] -> [3,4,1] -> [1,3] -> [1]. The survivor is 1.

questions.text: A queue is built on an ArrayList and dequeues with list.remove(0). What is the cost of one dequeue?
options: O(n), because every remaining element shifts one slot left
O(1), because only the first element is touched
O(log n), because the list is halved
O(n^2), because each shift is itself a removal
questions.answer: O(n), because every remaining element shifts one slot left
questions.explanation: Removing at index 0 of an array-backed list shifts all n-1 others. ArrayDeque or a circular buffer gives O(1) dequeue instead.

coding.title: Queue Command Simulator
coding.description: Simulate a queue of integers. Process the commands in order: ENQ x adds x at the back; DEQ removes the front and prints it; FRONT prints the front without removing; SIZE prints the current size. If DEQ or FRONT is used on an empty queue print EMPTY instead.
coding.inputDescription: Line 1: n, the number of commands. Next n lines: one command each (ENQ x, DEQ, FRONT or SIZE).
coding.outputDescription: One line for every DEQ, FRONT and SIZE command, in order.
coding.constraints: 1 <= n <= 20000, |x| <= 1000000, at least one command is not ENQ
